title: Stock Market Today Live: Gift Nifty at 25,260 signals weak opening for domestic markets - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live Updates: Find here all the live updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 18th November 2026.

Indian stock markets are likely to open on a weak note on Wednesday amid mixed global cues. Analysts expect the market to remain in consolidation mode after a sharp recovery from recent lows. As the result season has almost comes to end, the focus has now shifted to global and domestic micro economic factors.

Meanwhile, Gift Nifty at 25,260 signals a gap down opening of about 120 points for Nifty.

Global cues are broadly favourable with Asian equities trading higher in early deal on Wednesday. Japan’s Nikkei 225 has advanced more than 0.50 per cent, while South Korea’s KOSPI has gained over 2 per cent, signalling an improvement in regional risk appetite even as Wall Street ended sharply lower last night.

Crypto markets struggled to build a sustained recovery following the recent sell-off. Bitcoin traded near $64,387, while Ethereum hovered around $1,804, leaving the $1,800 level in focus. Total crypto market capitalisation stood near $2.18 trillion. The CoinMarketCap 20 Index declined 0.53% over 24 hours to 130.63, reflecting continued weakness across major assets.

ETF flows remained subdued. The supplied tracker recorded net crypto ETF outflows of $28.97 million on November 17, with Bitcoin funds losing approximately $29 million. Ethereum funds attracted around $1 million, offering a modest offset. The return to withdrawals highlights the fragility of institutional demand following the previous session’s inflows.

Liquidity conditions also warrant attention. According to the article excerpt, stablecoin supply contracted by approximately $17 billion over 30 days to $244 billion. Such a decline can indicate reduced capital available within the ecosystem, although it does not directly measure investors’ willingness to buy. The reported rise in the US 10-year Treasury yield to approximately 5.15% adds pressure by increasing the relative appeal of government debt.

Derivatives positioning showed renewed activity. The reported perpetual open interest is of $326.55 billion. Increasing perpetual exposure alongside subdued prices could leave markets vulnerable to further liquidation-driven volatility. Separately, an earlier liquidation window of approximately 1.7–2 billion has predominantly affected long positions.

Bitcoin’s recent low near $62,000 remains a key downside reference, while a sustained move above $65,000 would help improve the immediate price picture. Ethereum’s ability to hold $1,800 remains important for sentiment beyond Bitcoin.

Indian government bonds could see mild gains in opening trades on Tuesday, tracking a decline in crude oil prices, but major moves are ‌unlikely due to concerns over further interest rate hikes in India and the US.

The benchmark ⁠6.94% 2036 bond yield is expected to move between 7.22% and 7.28%, according to a private-bank trader, after ending at 7.2528% ‌on Tuesday. ( Reuters)

The Indian rupee is poised to extend its outperformance among Asian peers on Wednesday, with a revival in foreign equity inflows helping ‌the currency weather weakness across regional markets.

A resurgence in foreign equity inflows and a more ⁠favourable oil price environment have put the rupee on a firm footing, powering a rally that took it to a ‌more than seven-month high on Tuesday.

The rupee is expected to open flat to slightly higher, having ‌settled at 93.47 to the dollar in ‌the ⁠previous session. The rupee has climbed 1.5% so ⁠far this month at a time when most regional peers have weakened against the dollar.

The currency has broken past the closely watched 93.60 level, a ‌key technical hurdle, potentially paving the way for further appreciation and extending its outperformance against Asian peers, bankers said. ( Reuters)

Nvidia forecasts $130 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, topping estimates as investors weigh strong AI demand, new chips and uncertainty over its next CEO now.

Oil prices fell on Wednesday on data showing an increase in US crude and fuel inventories last week, although ongoing US-Iran attacks and ‌disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz limited losses.

US West Texas Intermediate futures fell 56 ⁠cents, or 0.65%, to $85.45 a barrel as of 0149 GMT, while Brent crude futures were trading down 16 cents, or 0.17%, at $92.98 a ‌barrel.

Crude stocks rose by 5.28 million barrels in the week ended November 13, market sources said ‌on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute, ‌while ⁠gasoline stocks rose by 5.12 million barrels and ⁠distillate inventories by 351,000 barrels. ( Reuters)

Indian stock markets are set to open weak amid mixed global cues, with Gift Nifty signaling a gap-down as consolidation dominates.

Stocks to watch on Nov 18: ArMee, IIFL Finance, RITES, Supreme Petrochem, Glenmark, Mankind Pharma, Ashok Buildcon, Advait Energy, Apollo Micro, Nykaa.

Support is in the ₹1,310-₹1,280 region. Fresh buyers are likely to coming in around this support zone and limit the downside. Moving average cross overs on the daily chart also strengthens the bullish case.
